messages.content: Return JSON with candidate_ids, critic and selection_rationale. Select exactly 5 evaluated aliases ordered by test priority. Give reasons that refer to the estimates and identify a weakness. New fluorescence measurements are unavailable until after submission. Reply with bare JSON. Limit critic and selection_rationale to 25 words each.

function.name: score_gfp_designs
function.description: Construct and score candidate GFP fluorescence sequences. Each design string is a menu alias followed by one space and its explicit colon-separated substitutions.

arguments.analyst: Comparing O1/O2 (single-plus-conservative edits, ~3.88-3.90) against O4/O5 (multiple nonconservative buried substitutions, ~1.30) suggests single conservative edits preserve brightness while clustered disruptive edits collapse it; menu single-edit options cluster near 3.58-3.63.
arguments.hypothesis: Single conservative menu edits (e.g., F46Y, N170H, E213K) retain high fluorescence comparable to O1/O2, whereas multi-edit candidates with L195P/charge-reversal clusters (C19, C21, C27) will score low, resembling O4/O5.

decision.analyst: Comparing O1/O2 (single-plus-conservative edits, ~3.88-3.90) against O4/O5 (multiple nonconservative buried substitutions, ~1.30) suggests single conservative edits preserve brightness while clustered disruptive edits collapse it; menu single-edit options cluster near 3.58-3.63.
decision.hypothesis: Single conservative menu edits (e.g., F46Y, N170H, E213K) retain high fluorescence comparable to O1/O2, whereas multi-edit candidates with L195P/charge-reversal clusters (C19, C21, C27) will score low, resembling O4/O5.
decision.critic: Estimates are model-fitted, not measured; C19-C27 low predictions rest on O4/O5 analogy with high uncertainty, so context effects unverified.
decision.selection_rationale: Prioritize top single conservative edits (C33, C13, C01) then low multi-edit clusters (C21, C27) to test the brightness-loss hypothesis.
